en.title: Longest Lexicographically Smallest Regular Expression (Pure Storage OA)
en.description: You are given uppercase strings x, y, z, each of length n. A regex is built from single uppercase letters or bracketed character classes, with no repeated letters inside a class, and the whole regex is concatenated position by position. Find the longest regex that matches both x and y but does not match z; if several answers have the same length, output the lexicographically smallest one; if none exists, output -1. The standard input/output protocol is added by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n (1≤n≤1000000); the next three lines are x, y, z in order, each containing exactly n uppercase English letters A-Z.
en.output: Output the longest, lexicographically smallest regex that matches x/y but does not match z; if there is no solution, output -1.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the full derivation, proof of correctness, and source notes.
hints: First find the positions that can reject z.
Full-alphabet classes maximize the length; when comparing candidates of the same length, pay attention to where the first shortened class appears.
